es: Escribir un diario de una semana en el extranjero, ordenado por días, con bloques léxicos (figure out, sort out, get the hang of), expresiones coloquiales y una estrategia de comunicación.

teaching.en: I landed on Sunday night, and my first diary entry is mostly about the taxi driver who did not stop talking.
teaching.es: Aterricé el domingo por la noche, y mi primera entrada de diario trata sobre todo del taxista que no paró de hablar.
teaching.explanationEs: Un diario se cuenta en pasado, con marcas de día (On Sunday…) y un tono personal.
segments: I landed on Sunday night, and my first diary entry is
mostly about the taxi driver who did not stop talking.
teaching.audioText: I landed on Sunday night, and my first diary entry is mostly about the taxi driver who did not stop talking.

teaching.en: On Monday I could not figure out the bus timetable, so I asked a stranger to rephrase her directions twice.
teaching.es: El lunes no pude averiguar el horario del autobús, así que le pedí a una desconocida que reformulara sus indicaciones dos veces.
teaching.explanationEs: Figure out: entender algo con esfuerzo. Pedir que rephrase es una estrategia de comunicación.
segments: On Monday I could not figure out the bus timetable,
so I asked a stranger to rephrase her directions twice.
teaching.audioText: On Monday I could not figure out the bus timetable, so I asked a stranger to rephrase her directions twice.

teaching.en: By Wednesday I had managed to sort out my phone contract, which is the only good news in my diary so far.
teaching.es: Para el miércoles había logrado resolver mi contrato de teléfono, que es la única buena noticia de mi diario hasta ahora.
teaching.explanationEs: Manage to + verbo: conseguir algo con esfuerzo. Sort out: resolver un problema práctico.
segments: By Wednesday I had managed to sort out my phone contract,
which is the only good news in my diary so far.
teaching.audioText: By Wednesday I had managed to sort out my phone contract, which is the only good news in my diary so far.

teaching.en: Culture shock hit me on Thursday; my diary says I could not get the hang of tipping, and I felt like a child.
teaching.es: El choque cultural me golpeó el jueves; mi diario dice que no lograba agarrarle el truco a las propinas y me sentí como un niño.
teaching.explanationEs: Get the hang of + algo: aprender a hacerlo con soltura. Culture shock: desorientación ante otra cultura.
segments: Culture shock hit me on Thursday; my diary says I could not
get the hang of tipping, and I felt like a child.
teaching.audioText: Culture shock hit me on Thursday; my diary says I could not get the hang of tipping, and I felt like a child.

teaching.en: When a shop assistant speaks too fast, I ask her to rephrase, and somehow we muddle through.
teaching.es: Cuando una dependienta habla demasiado rápido, le pido que lo reformule, y de algún modo nos las arreglamos.
teaching.explanationEs: Muddle through: salir adelante sin hacerlo bien ni con método, pero sin rendirse.
segments: When a shop assistant speaks too fast, I ask
her to rephrase, and somehow we muddle through.
teaching.audioText: When a shop assistant speaks too fast, I ask her to rephrase, and somehow we muddle through.

teaching.en: A week after I landed, I have pretty much settled in, and I can finally catch up on sleep and write a happier diary.
teaching.es: Una semana después de llegar, ya me he instalado más o menos, y por fin puedo recuperar el sueño y escribir un diario más alegre.
teaching.explanationEs: Settle in: adaptarse a un lugar nuevo. Catch up on + algo: recuperar lo que te faltaba.

prompt.es: ¿Qué petición es la más natural para aclarar lo que no entendiste?

choices.text: Sorry, you speak wrong, say it again.
Sorry, could you rephrase that, please?
Sorry, I am not understanding; repeat it me.

feedback.es: Could you rephrase that? es una petición cortés y natural; las otras dos tienen errores de gramática y de tono.

hint.es: Busca la frase cortés con could you…

origin.text: A shop assistant speaks very fast, and you have only understood half of what she has said about the delivery.

prompt.es: Completa: «No logré averiguar el horario del autobús, así que pedí ayuda.»

feedback.es: Figure out + algo significa entender o descubrir algo con esfuerzo.

hint.es: Verbo que significa «descubrir» y forma un phrasal con out.

origin.text: On my first morning, I could not ___ out the bus timetable, so I asked a stranger to explain it to me.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por fin le agarré el truco al sistema de autobuses.»

answer.text: I finally got the hang of the bus system

feedback.es: Get the hang of + algo expresa que por fin lo dominas.

hint.es: Empieza con I finally y termina con the bus system.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo se las arregló la hablante en la oficina de correos.

choices.text: She asked the clerk to repeat it more slowly, and they understood at once.
She bought the tickets only after a colleague translated.
She asked the clerk to rephrase it and added gestures.

feedback.es: Pidió que reformulara y completó con gestos: la estrategia de comunicación y el muddle through; no le bastó con que repitiera más despacio.

origin.audio: Tuesday. The thing is, I could not understand a word at the post office. The clerk was speaking so fast that I asked her to rephrase it, and in the end we muddled through with gestures and a lot of smiling. Mind you, I managed to buy the tickets. Anyway, it's not like I expected it to be easy.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del diario con su función.

pairs: I can't quite catch that; could you rephrase it?
By Friday I had pretty much settled in.
The thing is, I had no idea where to go.
On Thursday, culture shock hit me.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función distinta en el diario: aclarar, valorar, plantear un problema y ordenar el relato.

pairs: I can't quite catch that; could you rephrase it?
By Friday I had pretty much settled in.
The thing is, I had no idea where to go.
On Thursday, culture shock hit me.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me llevó una semana agarrarle el truco al dinero; ahora pago sin mirar.»

feedback.es: Get the hang of + algo significa aprender a manejarlo con soltura.

origin.text: Every shop used different notes and I kept paying too much. It took me a week to get the ___ of the money; now I pay without looking.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la autora sobre su progreso.

choices.text: She is quietly proud of how far she has come.
She is very happy with her progress and plans to tell her mother.
She finds the language easy now that she has settled.

feedback.es: Dice que está chuffed pero que no se lo diría a su madre, y compara el lunes con hoy: orgullo discreto ante su progreso.

origin.audio: Friday. It is the end of my first week, and I am writing this on the train, so forgive the handwriting. On Monday I could not even buy a ticket. Today I negotiated a flat deposit in two languages, well, one and a half. To be honest, I am chuffed, although I would never say so to my mother, because she would tell everybody. Mind you, on Wednesday night I was so homesick that I read my old messages twice. Anyway, I have pretty much settled in. The plan for tomorrow is simple: sleep until noon.

prompt.es: ¿Qué problema de registro tiene esta entrada de diario?

choices.text: It names too many problems, so the main complaint gets lost.
Formal letter phrases clash with slang, so the tone is uneven.
It switches to the future, which makes the events hard to follow.

feedback.es: El saludo y la despedida de carta formal chocan con la jerga (knackered, gutted, no worries): el tono no es coherente; el problema no es el número de quejas ni el futuro.

origin.text: Tuesday. Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to inform you that I am knackered. The thing is, the landlord failed to sort out the heating, and I am absolutely gutted. Yours faithfully, Ana. Anyway, tomorrow I will try to get the hang of the bus, no worries.

prompt.es: Completa: «Pedí al camarero que reformulara su pregunta, y la repitió más despacio.»

feedback.es: Ask someone to rephrase es una estrategia para que te lo digan de otra manera.

origin.text: When the waiter spoke too fast, I asked him to ___ his question, and he repeated it more slowly with a smile.

prompt.es: Escribe tu diario de una semana en otro país, por días y con bloques y coloquialismos.

answer.text: Sunday. I landed at nine, and the taxi driver talked for the whole ride. I was completely knackered, so I went straight to bed. Monday. The thing is, I could not figure out the bus timetable. I asked a stranger to rephrase her directions twice, and apparently the bus was the wrong one anyway. Bummer! Wednesday. I managed to sort out my phone contract. To be honest, I pretty much guessed the forms, but no worries, the assistant was kind. Thursday. Culture shock hit me. I could not get the hang of tipping, and I felt bewildered in a restaurant full of people shouting. Saturday. It drizzled all day, so I stayed in and wrote this diary. Mind you, I am starting to settle in, and I can finally catch up on sleep. Anyway, it was a bustling, awesome week.
accepted: Sunday. I landed at nine, and the taxi driver talked for the whole ride. I was completely knackered, so I went straight to bed. Monday. The thing is, I could not figure out the bus timetable. I asked a stranger to rephrase her directions twice, and apparently the bus was the wrong one anyway. Bummer! Wednesday. I managed to sort out my phone contract. To be honest, I pretty much guessed the forms, but no worries, the assistant was kind. Thursday. Culture shock hit me. I could not get the hang of tipping, and I felt bewildered in a restaurant full of people shouting. Saturday. It drizzled all day, so I stayed in and wrote this diary. Mind you, I am starting to settle in, and I can finally catch up on sleep. Anyway, it was a bustling, awesome week.

Monday. I landed late, and the airport was chaos. On Tuesday I could not figure out the ticket machine, so I asked a man to rephrase what he was saying, and we muddled through with gestures. Bummer, I missed my bus! On Wednesday, to be honest, I felt homesick, but I managed to sort out my room with the landlady. Thursday. I am slowly getting the hang of the coffee shop, and the waiter says my accent is nice. Mind you, he says it to everybody. By Saturday I had pretty much settled in, and on Sunday I slept until noon. Anyway, it was a tiring but awesome first week. On Friday, a neighbour invited me for tea, and I could only make out half of what she said, but I got the gist of it, and we had a lovely evening.

feedback.es: Un buen diario ordena los días, combina bloques del habla con coloquialismos y deja ver una estrategia de comunicación.

origin.text: Escribe el diario de tu primera semana en un país nuevo (al menos 125 palabras; ideal, 200): ordena los días (On Monday…), usa tres bloques (figure out, sort out, get the hang of, settle in, muddle through…), dos expresiones coloquiales (to be honest, mind you, bummer…) y una estrategia de comunicación (pedir que lo reformulen).

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra la autora ante el camarero?

choices.text: She is embarrassed by her mistake and doubts that she will improve.
She is angry because she thinks the waiter was mocking her accent.
Mixed feelings: grateful for the help, frustrated by the lost chance.

feedback.es: Quiere agradecerle y a la vez tirarle el menú: agradece la ayuda, pero le frustra perder la oportunidad de practicar.

origin.text: Thursday. I tried to order lunch in the new language, and the waiter answered in English. I felt like thanking him and throwing the menu at him at the same time. Mind you, my sentence had been perfect until the last word. Tomorrow I will try again, and this time I will not apologise before I speak.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nos las arreglamos con gestos y una sonrisa.»

answer.text: We muddled through with gestures and a smile

feedback.es: Muddle through + with + recursos describe salir adelante con lo que se tiene.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ya estoy bastante instalado: conozco las tiendas y a los vecinos.»

feedback.es: Pretty much significa casi o más o menos, y suaviza la afirmación.

origin.text: After a week I have ___ much settled in: I know the shops, the bus route and even my neighbours' names.
